title: Closedness of the trivial-fibre locus in a proper geometrically integral family with a section
statement: Let f:P→S be a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-over-base], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with geometrically integral fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Suppose f has a section σ [def-pc-section]. For any invertible module L [def-sc-invertible-module] on P, the set of s∈S such that the pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] of L to P_s over Spec κ(s) [def-weil-residue-field] is trivial is closed.

proof.text: Geometrically integral fibres are geometrically reduced and geometrically connected. Apply the proper-flat global-sections theorem to obtain universally trivial structure-sheaf pushforward.

An invertible source-library module gives an invertible sheaf of modules, hence a finite locally free module. Apply the universal Picard-locus theorem to L, obtaining an immersion j:T→S of finite presentation and its universal factorization property.
The closed Picard-locus theorem makes j a closed immersion under the geometrically integral hypothesis.
The section σ and the universal factorization property identify the image of j with the trivial-fibre locus by the range lemma. A closed immersion is a closed embedding, whose image is closed.
